vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED — "SQL Injection (discovered parameter \"search\" on /api/users)", CRITICAL, confidence:high, real evidence
vulnerabilities.notes: Initially MISSED on the first real scan: server/redTeam/sqlInjection.ts's/server/paramFuzzer.ts's SQL_ERROR_SIGNATURE regex had no pattern matching better-sqlite3's actual raw error text ("near \"X\": syntax error") — it only had "SQLite3::"/"SQLiteException", which are PHP/Java driver class-name prefixes that never appear in a real Node app. Fixed in this session (both files) and re-verified detecting.

vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED — "Reflected XSS (discovered parameter \"name\" on /profile)", HIGH, confidence:high, real evidence. Worked on the very first scan, no fix needed.
DETECTED — "Stored XSS (discovered form field \"text\" on /api/comments)", CRITICAL, confidence:high, real evidence
vulnerabilities.notes: Initially MISSED: server/storedXss.ts only re-checked the form's action URL and the site root for the persisted payload — never the page the form was actually found ON, which for a REST-style split (form on /post/1, action /api/comments) is neither. Added InjectableTarget.discoveredOnPage (stamped by server/crawler.ts's extractForms) and had displayCandidates() include it; re-verified detecting. Also had to fix a fixture bug: the form had no postId field, so the crawler's raw POST (bypassing this page's own onsubmit JS) 400'd before ever storing anything.

vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED — "Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)", CRITICAL, confidence:high, real evidence. Worked on the very first scan (with bolaIdentities supplied), no fix needed.
DETECTED — "Predictable Session Token (Weak Seed Hash)", CRITICAL, real evidence: an exact byte-for-byte hash match against the live captured token.
vulnerabilities.notes: Closed via a new, deliberately narrow probe (server/redTeam/weakSessionToken.ts), NOT generic statistical entropy analysis — entropy testing was considered and rejected for this exact case: MD5's output is uniformly distributed regardless of input entropy, so a hash of a weak seed is statistically indistinguishable from a real CSPRNG output. What actually works: with real credentials the CALLER explicitly supplies (never guessed — matches the trust model of authHeader/bolaIdentities, does not reopen prd.md's 'no autonomous login-form crawling' non-goal), log in exactly once, then try to reproduce the captured token OFFLINE from a small set of common (seed, algorithm) recipes across a short timestamp window. An exact match is definitive proof, not a probabilistic guess. New scan option `loginCredentials` threaded through routes/scans.ts -> scanWorker.ts -> scanner.ts. Along the way, fixed a real crash in this fixture's own auth.js (better-sqlite3 throws, not just fails to match, when a bound parameter isn't a string — hit once /login became a fuzzed discovered-form target) and reordered the probe to run before discovered-parameter fuzzing so it gets a clean shot at the login rate limiter.

vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED — "Exposed User Object Endpoint", CRITICAL, real evidence quoting the leaked field, endpoint:/admin/users
vulnerabilities.notes: Initially MISSED: server/apiProbes.ts's exposed-user-object check only tried ONE fixed path (/api/v1/users/admin) and only understood a single JSON object, not a list. Broadened to a small candidate-path list (EXPOSED_USER_OBJECT_PATHS) including /admin/users, and made the marker extraction array-aware (checks the first element of a JSON array too — a 'list every user' admin panel is exactly this shape). Reuses the caller-supplied authHeader that was already threaded through, so this also required passing a top-level authHeader on the scan (not just bolaIdentities) to reach an endpoint gated behind 'some session exists'.

vulnerabilities.actualResult: DETECTED — "Exposed Credential Signature (Stripe Secret Key)", CRITICAL, endpoint:http://127.0.0.1:4101/api/settings
vulnerabilities.notes: Initially MISSED: SAST secret-signature scanning (server/staticAnalysis.ts's analyzeSecrets) only ever ran over the root page's HTML — a JSON endpoint discovered by the crawler was fetched (for parameter mining) but its body was discarded unread whenever the content-type wasn't text/html. Added InjectableTarget-adjacent CrawlCapture (server/crawler.ts) so the crawler captures EVERY fetched response body/headers regardless of content type, then server/scanner.ts runs analyzeSecrets AND the cookie-flag check against every capture, not just the root. The finding's endpoint now names which page actually leaked it (server/findings.ts maps sf.file → Finding.endpoint when it's a URL).
